items.title: How Many Shares of Duke Energy, Southern Company or WEC Energy Pay $1,000 a Month in Dividends?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysA hypothetical retiree would need about $364,600 of Duke Energy, $374,800 of Southern Company or $374,900 of WEC Energy Group to collect $1,000 a month in dividends at today’s prices. All three cover their dividends comfortably, paying out 67% to 68% of normalized earnings in fiscal 2025, with Southern Company the least covered.

items.summary: Southern Company has completed a US$1.75b composite equity units offering, issuing 35,000,000 equity derivative units at US$50 each with a US$0.75 discount per security and a US$875m principal amount allocated twice within the structure. items.title: Southern (SO) Stock Looks About Right On Current Earnings
items.summary: Southern has delivered steady gains for long term holders. items.title: These 4 Utility Stocks Pay Dividends While AI Drives Electricity Demand Higher
items.summary: Four regulated power giants are cashing in on the data center boom, but only some of their dividends look built to last. One has already cut its payout, and another carries a risk that could hit shareholders first.

items.title: $75,000 in These 5 Dividend Stocks Could Pay More Than $1,700 a Year Across 5 Sectors
items.summary: When one industry stumbles, a retiree's dividend checks can shrink overnight. One approach spreads five equal bets across very different corners of the market, and the pick with the highest payout is not the one most investors would guess.

items.title: Investors Buy Unusually Large LEAP Options in Southeastern Utility, Southern Company
items.summary: Investors have bought huge, unusual amounts of long-dated calls (i.e., LEAPs) in a utility benefiting from strong corporate demand - Southern Co. (SO). These LEAPs show investors love SO stock for the long term.
